Subject: Re: Redshifts shifted after upgrade to lumenfit 2.5.0?

@kpd_wrangler Yes, I did read the changelog. The only relevant entry is “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812).” Nothing there says that a default changed or that existing fits would produce different redshifts.

I have now traced this to PR #812. It changed the `LineList.__init__` default from `wave_frame='air'` to `wave_frame='vacuum'`. My spectra are wavelength-calibrated in air and my config does not explicitly set `wave_frame`, so 2.5.0 handles the rest wavelengths differently. At 6563 Å, the vacuum/air wavelength ratio is about 1.00028, corresponding to roughly 83 km/s and exactly the systematic Δz ≈ −0.00028 I reported. Explicitly setting `LineList(..., wave_frame='air')` restores the 2.4.3 behavior.

“Works for me” does not test this configuration. If your data are already vacuum-calibrated, or your radio workflow does not use this air/vacuum conversion, I would not expect you to see a difference. Also, @m_okonkwo reports a similar offset on long-slit data above, so this is not limited to my setup.

I am frustrated that this was marked solved and attributed to my calibration or config without checking that case. Because the report was dismissed, I spent two days rechecking my wavelength calibration and re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra unnecessarily.

Could a maintainer please reopen this thread? This is a behavior-changing default, not merely an internal refactor. Please add an explicit note to the 2.5.0 section of `CHANGES.md`, and consider a warning or migration notice when `wave_frame` is not explicitly set.

Workaround for anyone finding this thread: for air-calibrated spectra, explicitly use:

`LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`

No arc-lamp re-reduction or change to the fitting configuration is needed.
